title: Akkadian Empire
capsule: The Akkadian Empire was the world's first multi-ethnic territorial empire, founded c. 2334 BC when Sargon of Akkad conquered the Sumerian city-states of southern Mesopotamia and established his capital Agade (precise location unknown) near the Tigris-Euphrates confluence in what is now central Iraq. At its peak under Sargon and his grandson Naram-Sin (r. c. 2254–2218 BC), imperial authority stretched from Elam in the east to the Mediterranean coast and possibly Anatolia in the west, unified by Akkadian-language administration and cuneiform bureaucracy. The empire faced severe internal revolts and external pressure from the Gutian mountain peoples of the Zagros; by c. 2154 BC the dynasty had collapsed, and control of Mesopotamia reverted to Sumerian city-states under the Third Dynasty of Ur.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core Mesopotamian heartland is attested by extensive cuneiform administrative texts; the claimed western extent to the Mediterranean and northern extent into Anatolia rests on royal inscriptions and their interpretation rather than administrative boundaries, and must be treated as maximum-reach rather than continuous control.
